defects.title: Processes, System Calls, Files, and Signals
defects.defect: The worker acknowledges a job before durable completion and exits immediately on `SIGTERM`, losing the in-flight result.
defects.requiredOracle: Graceful case: clean exit, no claim after the signal, and a completed or explicitly recoverable job. Abrupt case: signal termination, no graceful-stop event, and recovery from durable spool state without losing the job.

defects.title: Identity, Permissions, Capabilities, and Service Supervision
defects.defect: The API runs as root and its executable directory is writable by the service account, allowing configuration compromise to become code execution.
defects.requiredOracle: Required writes succeed; code, unit, and private-key writes fail; effective UID/GID and capability sets match policy; no service has a login shell; the units stop cleanly.

defects.title: CPU, Memory, Scheduling, Namespaces, and cgroups
defects.defect: The worker has no memory ceiling, and readiness remains green while host memory pressure causes unrelated services to stall.
defects.requiredOracle: Effective controls are visible in the cgroup, throttling or memory events change as predicted, the experiment exits within its bound, and unrelated Atlas components remain observable.

defects.title: Storage, Filesystems, I/O, and Durability
defects.defect: A result is renamed into place but the parent directory is never synchronized, so the program overstates its crash-durability guarantee.
defects.requiredOracle: Readers observe only complete old or new results; failed staging leaves no final partial object; restore reproduces expected state without reading the live directory.

defects.title: IP, Routing, Transport, and Sockets
defects.defect: An administrative endpoint binds to `0.0.0.0` because the developer confused “reachable by the proxy” with “reachable by every interface.”
defects.requiredOracle: Listener address and route evidence predict success or refusal; no administrative or worker listener becomes external; IPv4 and IPv6 behavior are recorded separately.

defects.title: DNS, HTTP, TLS, and PKI
defects.defect: The client disables certificate verification to “fix” a hostname mismatch, converting a naming error into loss of peer authentication.
defects.requiredOracle: Each failure is classified as DNS, TCP, TLS chain, validity, hostname, or HTTP host policy. No repair uses `-k` or an unverified context.

defects.title: Firewalls, NAT, Proxies, and Load Balancing
defects.defect: The API trusts any client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`, allowing an external caller to impersonate a private source address.
defects.requiredOracle: Spoofed identity is absent, GET attempts are bounded, POST has one attempt, the edge returns 503, and firewall results match the declared flow matrix.

defects.title: Virtualization, Images, Boot, and Cloud Compute
defects.defect: A startup script writes a long-lived cloud credential from user data into a world-readable file and assumes the instance hostname is permanent identity.
defects.requiredOracle: Replacement has a new instance identity, exact release/config identity, restored durable results, no secret in user data, and a passing verified request.

defects.title: Cloud Primitives, Identity, and Failure Domains
defects.defect: The architecture calls a single-zone VM and attached disk “highly available” because the cloud provider itself operates multiple zones.
defects.requiredOracle: No provider name is treated as semantic equivalence; static keys are rejected; single-zone dependencies block zone-tolerance claims; each resource has an owner and evidence route.

defects.title: Production Host Engineering and Final Defense
defects.defect: Readiness reports success while durable storage is read-only, so the proxy continues to send mutating traffic to a process that cannot keep its promise.
defects.requiredOracle: Readiness and routing react truthfully, durable jobs remain complete or recoverable, verified TLS returns, baseline tour passes, and post-clean manifests verify exactly.
